chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, who said, Abu al-Walid Hassan ibn Ziyad al-Sayqal said, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
The one whose tongue is truthful, his deed becomes pure; and the one whose intention is good, his livelihood is increased; and the one who is righteous to his family, his lifespan is extended.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits of truthfulness, good intention, and family righteousness in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a causal link between internal sincerity and external divine blessings, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the unity of belief and action. It highlights that truthfulness of the tongue purifies deeds, while righteous intention and familial piety specifically invite increased provision and longevity, underscoring the practical spiritual benefits of moral integrity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam who said, ‘Abu Al Waleed Hassan Bin Ziyad Al Sayqal said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘The one who is truthful of his tongue would purify his deed, and the one who is good of intention would increase in his livelihood, and the one of goodly righteousness with his family members, there would be an extension for him in his life-span’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam who has said that abu al-Walid, Hassan ibn Ziyad al-Sayqal has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Making one’s tongue speak the truth purifies one’s deeds. Having good intentions increases one’s livelihood. One who betters his kind deeds toward his family is granted longevity in his life.’”
